subject: Inference needs & SLA confirmation for Atlas Retail
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@atlas-retail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Inference needs & SLA confirmation for Atlas Retail

Alex / Sandra — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared understanding before the SE deep-dive. TL;DR: primary needs are p95 latency improvement for streaming suggestions, predictable concurrency during peak campaigns, and an incremental path to lower per-token cost without sacrificing UX.

Key pain points you shared:
- Streaming suggestions currently show perceived lag for users: p95 ~800–1,000ms under peak conditions.
- Thundering spikes during marketing promos: backend CPU fallbacks cause jitter and long tails.
- Concurrency pressure: engineering sees 500–700 simultaneous live sessions on promo days (goal is to support 800+ without degradation).

Current stack (what I captured):
- On-prem inference with Triton fronting several model variants (FP16 and CPU fallback).
- Redis used for short-term caching of recent prefixes.
- Traffic pattern: big daily peaks around PST prime time + large weekly promos.

Stated success criteria (please confirm if I missed anything):
1) Streaming p95 for search suggestions <= 200ms for the primary UX model.
2) Sustain 800 concurrent active sessions and 1,200 rps at peak with graceful degradation to a cheaper model if needed.
3) Maintain quality within a <=5% regression on top-3 suggestion relevance compared to current model.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Can you share a short architecture diagram (png) and a 24h traffic sample (timestamps + inferred rps/p95 if possible) before our deep-dive?
- Marissa and I propose a technical deep-dive to go over traces, KV cache behavior, and batching strategies. Suggested window: Nov 9–11, 60–75 minutes.
- I'll prepare a short capacity checklist for the session (batching knobs, KV cache hit expectations, quantization options).

Attachments: none in this message — please send the arch diagram when convenient (Alex mentioned he could share).

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0189
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@atlas-retail.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@atlas-retail.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inference needs & SLA confirmation for Atlas Retail

Kimberly — thanks for the clear notes. Confirming the bullets and adding a couple of numbers to make the deep-dive productive:

Corrections / confirmations:
- p95 during normal traffic is ~220ms; during promo spikes it jumps to 800–1,000ms (matches your note).
- Peak concurrency: sustained ~550, but short spikes up to ~720 when promo emails land. We want headroom to 800 sustained for next season.
- Average token length for suggestions is small (8–15 tokens), but we have a long-tail of larger requests when customers use the freeform search box.

I'll attach the architecture diagram and a sampled 12-hour p95 CSV for yesterday's promo run. The diagram shows Triton on an internal GPU cluster, with a scaled CPU fallback pool and Redis layer for recent prefixes.

Attached: atlas-current-arch.png and sample-p95-20261107.csv (see Drive link inlined).

We'll be available Nov 10 in the afternoon (PST) for a deep-dive. If Nov 9/11 are better for you, we can adjust.

Alex Carter
Product Lead, Search
Atlas Retail
alex.carter@atlas-retail.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@atlas-retail.com>, Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@atlas-retail.com>

Date: 2026-11-09T09:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inference needs & SLA confirmation for Atlas Retail — SE deep-dive prep

Alex / Sandra — Marissa from the SE team here. Thanks for the artifacts, Alex — that helps a lot. I attached a short checklist we’ll use to validate capacity and surface low-risk wins before a proof-of-concept.

Proposed 60-minute deep-dive agenda (Nov 10, 1:30pm PST):
1) Quick recap (5m) — confirm traffic windows and success criteria.
2) Walkthrough of arch diagram & sample traces (15m).
3) Live review of p95 distribution by model + token length (15m).
4) Batching, KV caching, and graceful fallback options — tradeoffs (15m).
5) Next steps & timeline for a short spike test / POC (10m).

Pre-work for Atlas (please upload to the shared Drive before the call):
- 24h p95 CSV with timestamps (already received — thank you).
- Token length distribution for suggestion requests.
- Any recent tracing snippets around promo spikes (span IDs).

Attachment: redwood-concurrency-sla-checklist.pdf (capacity checklist, batching and cache tests).

If that time works I'll send a calendar invite and a short link to a sandbox cluster we can use for a quick 30-minute spike test.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
From: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@atlas-retail.com>

Subject: Re: Inference needs & SLA confirmation for Atlas Retail

Marissa / Kimberly — 1:30pm PST on Nov 10 works for us, thanks. A couple of procurement/compliance asks up front so we can loop in our infra team:
- Can you share your SOC 2 report or an SOC 2 letter of attestation and high-level data residency controls?
- We will need a short procurement checklist and a proposed timeline for a pilot (30-day sandbox + 2-week spike test).

Also, can the sandbox include a streaming demo of the suggestions UI so our PM can validate perceived latency improvements? If you can provision that before the call it would be ideal.

CCing procurement at procurement@atlas-retail.com (they will send official docs if required). Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Thanks —
Sandra Lopez
CTO, Atlas Retail
sandra.lopez@atlas-retail.com
